_: Category-based semantic-search eval — SET #3 ('Eval Dataset #2 / Ground Truth').
20 queries over 18 distinct landmark Iowa cases, same four query styles as
caselaw_eval_queries_categories.json:
A  Pure fact-pattern / narrative  (messy real-world scenario -> holding)
B  Abstract legal concept         (formal jargon, no narrative overlap)
C  Fragmentary / citation / name  (short token distributions)
D  Adversarial / hard-rerank      (shared keywords, different rule)
'area' carries the testing CATEGORY so eval_caselaw's by-area report is a
per-category breakdown. 'legal_area'/'category'/'distractor' are extra fields
the harness ignores; 'distractor' names the case that MUST be outranked.
ALL 20 target_cluster values were resolved against the DB on 2026-06-07 and the
claimed holding was verified against the opinion body_text. Resolution notes:
- Recent cases (Wright 2021, Burnett 2023, Garrison 2022, Standard Water 2020)
have EMPTY source_metadata.citations AND no ReporterCitation row (the ongoing
CourtListener scrape does not populate reporter cites the way the historical
bulk did), so they were resolved by case_name + date_filed, not by cite.
- Those recent cases are stored as DUPLICATE clusters, all fully embedded and
therefore all competing in retrieval: Wright x3 (4893114/4894883/5290145),
canonical (lowest-id) cluster is the target; a sibling duplicate outranking
it is a measurement artifact (see eval finding #3), not a retrieval failure.
- Mitchell v. City of Cedar Rapids (#12 target) is a DASH-cam (not body-cam)
Chapter 22 public-records case; the motorist (Jerime Mitchell) was rendered
quadriplegic, not killed. Case/cite resolve correctly; query kept verbatim.
- The source set's Kragnes v. City of Des Moines cite (710 N.W.2d 242) is
WRONG (that cite is Lange v. Iowa Dep't of Revenue); real Kragnes is
714 N.W.2d 632. Kragnes is not a query target, so it does not affect scoring.
run: python manage.py eval_caselaw --rerank --verbose \
--queries apps/corpus/data/caselaw_eval_queries_categories2.json \
--out benchmarks/caselaw/caselaw_categories2.json
